title: First and Last Position

concept.title: Two borders around a block of equal values
body: All copies of `x` in a sorted array form one block. Its left border is the first index with `a[i] >= x` (the **lower bound** of `x`) and the index right after its right border is the first index with `a[i] >= x + 1` (the lower bound of `x + 1`, for integers).
If both borders are the same index, the block is empty and `x` is missing. The difference `after - first` is also the number of copies of `x`.

statement: Given a sorted array (non-decreasing) and a number `x`, print the index of the first and the index of the last occurrence of `x`, counting from 0. If `x` does not occur, print `-1 -1`.
inputFormat: The second line has the sorted array.
outputFormat: Print two integers separated by a space.
hints: Write a function that finds the first index with `a[i] >= v`.
The first occurrence is at `lower_bound(x)` if that element equals x.
The last occurrence is just before `lower_bound(x + 1)`.

solution.complexity: Time O(log n) per search, space O(1).
